title: Skylines, Clipping, Underlines & Intent
description: Extruded type skylines, clip vs hidden overflow, animated native underlines, hover-intent timing, and accordions that answer find-in-page.

drops.title: Type as Architecture
drops.description: A word sampled into a grid, then extruded into towers that rise on a staggered timeline and keep swaying.
drops.concept: Each letter is rasterised to a low-resolution occupancy grid on an offscreen canvas, and every filled cell becomes an isometric tower whose height comes from a deterministic hash. The build-up delay is a function of grid position, so the word assembles left-to-right rather than popping in. A flat plane viewed isometrically collapses at 45°, so the camera sways within a readable arc and the footprint is re-fitted to the canvas every frame.
drops.source: Serhii Polyvanyi — “Turning Names Into Digital Architecture with Three.js” (Codrops)

interaction.mouse: Type up to three words to rebuild all three skylines; drag density, tower height and orbit sliders.
interaction.click: Click a skyline to re-seed and replay its build-up; Rebuild re-seeds all three.
interaction.touch: Tap any skyline to rebuild; the three scenes stack to one column.

drops.title: Clip Is Not Hidden
drops.description: overflow:hidden quietly makes a scroll container; overflow:clip does not — and it brings a licence to bleed.
drops.concept: A box set to overflow:hidden becomes a scroll container: script can scroll it, focus can scroll it, and any position:sticky inside it sticks to that box instead of the page. overflow:clip simply clips, and unlocks overflow-clip-margin so a hover lift or shadow can escape a set distance while the other axis stays clipped. Four panels prove each claim live, including a table of two-value overflow declarations read straight out of the visitor's own engine — where a scrolling value silently rewrites visible to auto.
drops.source: Web Standards — “What's new in Chrome 153” (overflow: scroll clip)

interaction.mouse: Hover a rail tile to watch the lift escape or get guillotined; scroll each list to see sticky work or fail.
interaction.click: Press “Scroll both boxes” to prove only the hidden box moves; drag the clip-margin slider.
interaction.touch: Swipe the rails horizontally; the comparison pairs stack to one column.

drops.title: Underline Choreography
drops.description: The browser's own underline is a length you can animate — and Chrome 154 adds two more knobs to the same decoration.
drops.concept: text-underline-offset is a real animatable length, so an underline can travel up to the baseline on hover instead of fading in, with no pseudo-element and correct wrapping across lines. Chrome 154 beta adds text-decoration-inset and text-decoration-skip-spaces on top; both are applied here behind @supports, and the panel disables the controls it cannot drive rather than pretending.
drops.source: Chrome 154 beta release notes — text-decoration-inset & text-decoration-skip-spaces

interaction.mouse: Hover the editorial links to pull each underline home; drag offset, thickness and parked-offset sliders.
interaction.click: Switch skip-spaces between all and none where supported.
interaction.touch: All sliders are touch-sized; the comparison grid stacks to one column.

drops.title: Hover Intent
drops.description: Two timers and a shared warm flag turn twitchy tooltips into ones that wait, then keep up.
drops.concept: An eager tooltip flashes at every cursor that merely passes through; a slow one feels broken. The pattern is a delay before the first open, a group-wide warm flag so neighbours then open instantly, and a grace window on close so travelling diagonally into the panel never dismisses it. Four instances share one implementation — avatar chips, a menu bar, inline table triggers, and a deliberately intent-free row for comparison — with a conic ring that renders the delay you are tuning.
drops.source: Abhishek Jakhar — “Tooltips need a delay, and then they need to skip it”

interaction.mouse: Sweep across a group and nothing opens; rest on one and it opens, then neighbours are instant.
interaction.click: Tune open delay, close grace and warm window; the panel reports whether the group is warm.
interaction.touch: A tap opens immediately — touch has no hover to disambiguate.

drops.title: Findable When Folded
drops.description: An accordion whose collapsed answers still answer find-in-page, via hidden=until-found and beforematch.
drops.concept: Collapsed content set with hidden="until-found" stays searchable by the browser's own find-in-page: on a match the browser fires beforematch, then unhides and scrolls to the panel. Listening for that event is the only chance to fix state CSS cannot see — without it the trigger's arrow still points sideways at an open answer. Firefox 148 and Safari 26.2 shipped it during 2026, so the pattern is finally dependable; a side-by-side with plain hidden shows exactly what searching loses, and a forty-row log adds content-visibility on top.
drops.source: Nathan Knowler — “Searchable, collapsible sections with hidden=until-found”

interaction.mouse: Click any question to fold or unfold it; compare the plain-hidden and until-found panels.
interaction.click: Press Ctrl/⌘+F and search a word that only exists inside a folded panel, or use Simulate a page find.
interaction.touch: Fully tappable; the simulate button covers browsers whose find UI is hard to reach.
